messages.content: You are Kimi Linear 48B-A3B Instruct running locally through a GGUF quant. Answer directly and note uncertainty.
Explain what makes Kimi Delta Attention different from standard attention in 5 bullets.

message.content:
- **Sliding-window locality**: Kimi Delta Attention only looks at a fixed-size “window” of recent tokens around the current position, instead of the full context, drastically cutting memory and compute.
- **Delta encoding**: It stores the attention scores relative to the current token (a “delta”) rather than absolute dot-product similarities, which reduces parameter count and improves efficiency.
- **Hierarchical compression**: The window is compressed into a small summary vector before being combined with the delta, so the model can still “see” farther context without holding all prior keys/values in memory.
- **Dynamic window size**: The window length can expand or shrink on the fly depending on how far back the model needs to look, balancing accuracy and cost.
- **Cache reuse**: Older keys/values are evicted from the cache once they fall out of the window, keeping memory usage bounded regardless of sequence length.
